The continuation is clear: White is winning by a huge margin after Kxd5. This is a **fork/double attack** motif—the king captures the undefended knight while the rook is attacked by the pawn on b5, but White wins material overall.

**Coaching Note (80 words max):**

You had an undefended knight on d5 that your king could capture. When you see an undefended enemy piece, always check if you can take it—even if your own piece gets attacked in reply. Here, Kxd5 wins the knight: after Black plays bxc4 (attacking your rook), you play Kxc4 and you're up a whole piece. The key lesson: if the material count favors you after the forced sequence, take the hanging piece. Always calculate the full recapture line.
